Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
import json

def solve_turnstile_and_fetch(page):
    # Navigate to openreview search page
    page.goto('https://openreview.net/search?query=ICML+2024+accepted', 
              wait_until='domcontentloaded', timeout=60000)
    page.wait_for_timeout(8000)
    
    # Try to wait for turnstile to solve
    try:
        page.wait_for_selector('form[name="challenge-form"]', timeout=15000)
        print("Found challenge form")
    except:
        print("No challenge form found, checking page")
    
    # Check page state
    content = page.content()
    if 'Verifying' in content:
        print("Still on verification page")
    
    # Get the data from the page using evaluate
    data = page.evaluate('''
        () => {
            return {
                title: document.title,
                bodyText: document.body.innerText.substring(0, 5000),
                hasPapers: document.querySelector('[class*="paper"]') !== null
            };
        }
    ''')
    print(f"Page state: {json.dumps(data, indent=2)[:1000]}")
    
    return data

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    context = browser.new_context(
        user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
        viewport={'width': 1920, 'height': 1080}
    )
    
    # Set navigator.webdriver to false
    context.add_init_script('Object.defineProperty(navigator, "webdriver", {get: () => false})')
    
    page = context.new_page()
    data = solve_turnstile_and_fetch(page)
    browser.close()
PYEOF

import json
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        context = browser.new_context(
            user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/125.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
            viewport={'width': 1920, 'height': 1080}
        )
        context.add_init_script('Object.defineProperty(navigator, "webdriver", {get: () => false})')
        page = context.new_page()
        
        # Try accessing specific venue pages
        urls = [
            'https://openreview.net/group?id=NeurIPS.cc/2024/Conference',
            'https://openreview.net/group?id=ICLR.cc/2025/Conference',
        ]
        
        for url in urls:
            print(f"\n=== Navigating to {url} ===")
            page.goto(url, wait_until='domcontentloaded', timeout=60000)
            page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
            
            # Check if verification needed
            body_text = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText.substring(0, 500)')
            if 'Verifying' in body_text:
                print("Need to wait for turnstile...")
                for i in range(30):
                    page.wait_for_timeout(1000)
                    bt = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText.substring(0, 500)')
                    if 'Verifying' not in bt:
                        print(f"Passed after {i}s")
                        break
                else:
                    print("Still verifying")
                    continue
            
            # Get the full page body text
            body = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText.substring(0, 10000)')
            print(f"Body preview: {body[:1000]}")
            
            # Try to scroll and wait for content
            page.evaluate('window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)')
            page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
            
            body2 = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText.substring(0, 10000)')
            print(f"After scroll: {body2[:500]}")
        
        browser.close()

run()

Human Expertise in Algorithmic Prediction
Rohan Alur ⋅ Manish Raghavan ⋅ Devavrat Shah
Dec 11, 10:00 AM - 10:20 AM
West Exhibition Hall C, B3
We introduce a novel framework for incorporating human expertise into algorithmic predictions. Our approach leverages human judgment to distinguish inputs which
 are *algorithmically indistinguishable*, or "look the same" to predictive algorithms. We argue that this framing clarifies the problem of human-AI collaboratio
n in prediction tasks, as experts often form judgments by drawing on information which is not encoded in an algorithm's training data. Algorithmic indistinguish
ability yields a natural test for assessing whether experts incorporate this kind of "side information", and further provides a simple but principled method for
 selectively incorporating human feedback into algorithmic predictions. We show that this method provably improves the performance of any feasible algorithmic p
redictor and precisely quantify this improvement. We find empirically that although algorithms often outperform their human counterparts *on average*, human jud
gment can improve algorithmic predictions on *specific* instances (which can be identified ex-ante). In an X-ray classification task, we find that this subset c
onstitutes nearly 30% of the patient population. Our approach provides a natural way of uncovering this heterogeneity and thus enabling effective human-AI colla
boration.

T-Cal: An Optimal Test for the Calibration of Predictive Models
Donghwan Lee ⋅ Xinmeng Huang ⋅ Hamed Hassani ⋅ Edgar Dobriban
2024 Poster
[
Poster

JMLR

Abstract
The prediction accuracy of machine learning methods is steadily increasing, but the calibration of their uncertainty predictions poses a significant challenge.
Numerous works focus on obtaining well-calibrated predictive models, but less is known about reliably assessing model calibration. This limits our ability to kn
ow when algorithms for improving calibration have a real effect, and when their improvements are merely artifacts due to random noise in finite datasets. In thi
s work, we consider detecting mis-calibration of predictive models using a finite validation dataset as a hypothesis testing problem. The null hypothesis is tha
t the predictive model is calibrated, while the alternative hypothesis is that the deviation from calibration is sufficiently large. We find that detecting mis-
calibration is only possible when the conditional probabilities of the classes are sufficiently smooth functions of the predictions. When the conditional class
probabilities are Holder continuous, we propose T-Cal, a minimax optimal test for calibration based on a debiased plug-in estimator of the
ℓ
2
-Expected Calibration Error (ECE). We further propose adaptive T-Cal, a version that is adaptive to unknown smoothness. We verify our theoretical findings with
a broad range of experiments, including with several popular deep neural net architectures and several standard post-hoc calibration methods. T-Cal is a practic
al general-purpose tool, which---combined with classical tests for discrete-valued predictors---can be used to test the calibration of virtually any probabilist
ic classification method.

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
import re, json, time

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True, args=['--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled'])
    context = browser.new_context(
        user_agent='Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/125.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
        viewport=dict(width=1920, height=1080)
    )
    context.add_init_script('Object.defineProperty(navigator, "webdriver", {get: function() { return false; }})')
    page = context.new_page()
    
    # Visit NeurIPS paper page first
    page.goto('https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/oral/97944', wait_until='domcontentloaded', timeout=60000)
    page.wait_for_timeout(3000)
    
    # Get the OpenReview URL
    or_url = page.evaluate('() => { const a = document.querySelector("a[href*=\"openreview\"]"); return a ? a.href : null; }')
    print(f"OpenReview URL: {or_url}")
    
    # Now navigate to OpenReview within same session
    # This should carry over any cookies
    page.goto(or_url, wait_until='domcontentloaded', timeout=60000)
    
    # Wait for Cloudflare to solve
    print("Waiting for Cloudflare...")
    solved = False
    for i in range(50):
        page.wait_for_timeout(1000)
        body = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText.substring(0, 200)')
        if 'Verifying' not in body and len(body) > 200:
            print(f"Cloudflare solved after {i+1}s")
            solved = True
            break
    
    if solved:
        page.wait_for_timeout(5000)
        # Get meta tags
        metas = page.evaluate('() => { const m = {}; document.querySelectorAll("meta[name]").forEach(t => { m[t.getAttribute("name")] = t.getAttribute("content"); }); return m; }')
        print("\nMeta tags:")
        for k, v in metas.items():
            if 'citation' in k.lower() or 'affil' in k.lower():
                print(f"  {k}: {v[:300]}")
        
        # Also get all text
        full = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText')
        print(f"\nPage text length: {len(full)}")
        print(f"First 2500:\n{full[:2500]}")
        
        # Save to file
        with open('/app/openreview_page.txt', 'w') as f:
            f.write(full)
        with open('/app/openreview_metas.json', 'w') as f:
            json.dump(metas, f, indent=2)
    else:
        body = page.evaluate('document.body.innerText.substring(0, 200)')
